title: Types, Strings, Input, and Validation
summary: Use scalar and composite types, strict function signatures, explicit conversion, null handling, filter functions, and validated input.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Types, Strings, Input, and Validation
Verify contracts with lint, runtime, and test evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: PHP supports scalar types, arrays, objects, null, unions, and typed function contracts. Strict types affect scalar argument coercion for calls made from that file; they do not validate external input automatically. Values from command-line arguments, forms, query strings, JSON, and databases remain untrusted. Validate presence, shape, range, and allowed values before constructing domain state. Use `filter_var` only for filters it actually supports, and distinguish missing data from valid zero or empty text. Avoid loose comparisons when types matter.
keyPoints: PHP supports scalar types, arrays, objects, null, unions, and typed function contracts.
commonMistakes: external data still needs runtime validation
loose comparison can equate surprising values

sections.heading: Worked PHP example
sections.content:
Predict types, failures, and output, then lint, run, and compare the evidence.

In practical software engineering with PHP, understanding runtime behavior, boundary cases, and diagnostic evidence is essential for reliable deployment.

codeExamples.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
$text = '19';
$age = filter_var($text, FILTER_VALIDATE_INT);
if ($age === false) { throw new InvalidArgumentException('age'); }
echo ($age + 1) . "\n";
